claim: Across five experiments on 17 models from five LLM series, reasoning ability scales with model size but item-level metacognitive sensitivity does not; in some series the smallest models show higher sensitivity than larger ones. ABSTRACT-ONLY (Crossref record of the OSF/PsyArXiv preprint).
stance_target: F: confidence discrimination is a distinct measured construct, not a by-product of capability; reasoning traces hurt self-evaluation
scope_conditions: 17 models, 5 series, non-code reasoning tasks; ABSTRACT-ONLY, posted 2026-01-06; full text on osf.io not fetched (host not allowed)
quoted_support: Although reasoning ability reliably scales with model size, metacognitive sensitivity does not; in some series, the smallest models even exhibit higher metacognitive sensitivity than their larger counterparts.

claim: Authors attribute the deviation to long, deterministic reasoning traces that boost performance but hinder accurate self-evaluation, and report that distilling traces into small models transfers the impairment. ABSTRACT-ONLY.
stance_target: L2: reasoning vs non-reasoning models differ in confidence discrimination
quoted_support: long and deterministic reasoning traces boost performance but hinder accurate self-evaluation. Furthermore, distilling the reasoning traces of large models into small models transfers the impairment in metacognitive sensitivity.
